text:
maria: heads up — after the GPU scale event in us-west-edge a few mins ago, svc/infer-headless DNS queries sometimes return NXDOMAIN. pods are Running though.

tim: I see the same. `kubectl get pods -n ml -l app=infer` shows pods on the new nodes. `dig infer-headless.ml.svc.cluster.local` returns NOERROR but no A records intermittently.

cheng: kube-proxy logs on one of the new nodes show repeated `conntrack: unable to restore conntrack table: table full`.

olivia: also getting 502/504 from the inference gateway for pods on those nodes — could be NAT ephemeral ports limiting egress to model storage S3.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled up 6 nodes to us-west-edge (gpu-rtx-a10) at 2026-03-18T12:18:32Z.

maria: ran `kubectl get endpointslices -n ml -l kubernetes.io/service-name=infer-headless -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'` — on some nodes there are 0 slices for the service. other nodes show expected slices.

tim: hmm that points to endpoint controller not reconciling quickly after node join. Could be kube-controller-manager CPU pressure. Any spikes in controller-manager metrics?

cheng: metrics show `workqueue_depth` spike for endpointSlice-controller and kube-proxy conntrack errors. suspect conntrack leak -> kube-proxy choking while reconciling rules.

olivia: quick mitigation ideas: 1) roll kube-proxy daemonset on new nodes 2) increase controller-manager `--concurrent-service-syncs` to 20 temporarily 3) scale out NAT appliance or widen ephemeral port range.

maria: rolling restart kube-proxy now on affected nodes: `kubectl rollout restart ds/kube-proxy -n kube-system --selector=node-role.kubernetes.io=edge=true`.

tim: while that's rolling, i'm opening ticket with cloud infra to bump NAT ephemeral ports and add one more NAT appliance in us-west-edge.

cheng: after restarting kube-proxy on node edge-12 I see conntrack errors cleared and endpointslice appeared: `kubectl get endpointslices -n ml -l kubernetes.io/service-name=infer-headless` shows slices distributed.

olivia: gateway 502s dropped to 0 after NAT scale-out. good sign.

maria: follow-ups: 1) add node-local-dns to edge nodes to reduce CoreDNS load and faster DNS convergence 2) add alert for EndpointSlice count drop per service 3) add preflight to autoscaler to stagger joins so controller-manager isn't overwhelmed.

tim: agree. i'll put up a PR for the alert rule and the autoscaler stagger change. cheng can you file a kube-controller-manager config change to bump concurrent-service-syncs?

cheng: will do. also proposing we reduce conntrack default timeout and increase table size on edge kernel config pool as a precaution.

maria: thanks all — marking this thread resolved once PRs land. :thumbsup:
